stem:
Wafa knows that lines $p$ and $q$ are parallel and that transversal $t$ cuts them. Angle $a$ between $p$ and $t$ measures $140^{\circ}$. Angle $x$ between $q$ and $t$ is the co-interior angle to angle $a$ on the same side of $t$.

Which claim about angle $x$ is correct?

options.text: Angle $x$ equals $40^{\circ}$, because co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^{\circ}$.
Report the words parallel lines as the measure of angle $x$.
Angle $x$ equals $40^{\circ}$, and that is only the angle next to angle $a$ on the straight line at $p$, with no use of the parallel.
Angle $x$ equals $140^{\circ}$, the printed measure of angle $a$.

teacher.key_rationale: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary, so $x=180^{\circ}-140^{\circ}=40^{\circ}$. Naming "parallel lines" as a measure, stopping at a local linear pair without the parallel, or copying $140^{\circ}$ miss that hinge.
